question.prompt: In the sixth, seventh, eighth, and ninth basketball games of the season, a player scored \(23,\) \(14,\) \(11,\) and \(20\) points, respectively. Her points-per-game average was higher after nine games than it was after the first five games. If her average after ten games was greater than \(18,\) what is the least number of points she could have scored in the tenth game?

solutions.explanation:
The unknown first five scores matter only through their total. Let that total be the nonnegative integer \(S\). The next four games contribute
\[
23+14+11+20=68
\]
points. The increase in her average means
\[
\frac{S+68}{9}>\frac S5.
\]
Multiplying by the positive number \(45\) preserves the inequality and gives
\[
5S+340>9S,
\qquad S<85.
\]
Since scores are integers, \(S\le84\). Thus her total after nine games is at most \(84+68=152\).

To average more than \(18\) points over ten games, her integer total must be at least \(181\). Therefore her tenth-game score must be at least
\[
181-152=29.
\]
This is attainable: first-five scores of \(16,17,17,17,17\) total \(84\), and then
\[
\frac{152}{9}>\frac{84}{5}.
\]
Scoring \(29\) in the tenth game gives an average of \(181/10>18\). The least possible score is therefore \(\boxed{29}\), choice \(\mathrm D\).
solutions.title: Bound the total before the tenth game
